rendered:
Yes. LOD values for both CD and UV–vis are given for only a pair of strains, and in both cases CD is lower. The authors say CD consistently achieved lower limit of detection (LOD) than UV–vis[1]. How much lower depends a lot on the strain:

1. P. aeruginosa: CD LOD OD600 =0.0034[2] versus UV–vis 0.0066[3]. CD is lower by an OD600 of 0.0032[4], which is about 48.5[5]% lower. Put another way, the UV–vis LOD is roughly 1.94[6] times the CD LOD.
2. L. monocytogenes: CD LOD 0.0123[7] versus UV–vis 0.0125[8]. CD is lower by only 0.0002[9], which is about 1.6[10]% lower, so the methods are almost the same for this strain.

All these values are OD600 units, not CFU/mL. The document doesn't give LODs for the other strains, such as E. coli and E. sakazakii, even though those were also tested across concentrations. Those LOD values come from the supplementary figures, which aren't part of this document.[11]
